jobs.title: Senior Hydrogeologist
jobs.description:
Senior Hydrogeologist – Commercial & Industrial Remediation Lead

California | Remote/Hybrid | $130,000–$180,000 base + performance bonus

Harper Harrison is supporting an established national environmental consultancy with the appointment of a Senior Hydrogeologist to help grow and deliver its California investigation and remediation portfolio.
This position combines technical leadership, project management and client development. It would suit an experienced California consultant who wants greater influence over client strategy and practice growth while remaining involved in project delivery.
You will not be expected to build from nothing. The business already has active projects, national-account relationships and a team of mid-level and junior professionals available to support delivery.

The Opportunity

Lead environmental investigation and remediation projects throughout California.
Develop relationships with larger commercial and industrial clients.
Target sectors including manufacturing, aerospace, energy and other complex industrial environments.
Manage project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing and technical deliverables.
Lead proposals, presentations and client-development activities.
Provide senior hydrogeologic guidance across site characterization and groundwater-remediation programs.
Mentor geologists, engineers, scientists and technical staff.
Work alongside national account and technical leaders to pursue larger strategic opportunities.
Help shape the growth of the California environmental practice.

Required Experience

Approximately 10–20 years of geology, hydrogeology or environmental consulting experience.
Active California Professional Geologist (PG) or Certified Hydrogeologist (CHg) credential.
Strong experience in contaminated-site investigation and environmental remediation.
Ability to perform and oversee hydrogeologic evaluations and groundwater investigations.
Successful project-management experience, including budget and team responsibility.
Demonstrated ability to develop client relationships, secure work or expand existing accounts.
Knowledge of California regulatory programs, including DTSC and California Water Boards.
Experience working within CERCLA and/or RCRA frameworks.
Ability to lead multidisciplinary technical teams and communicate effectively with clients and regulators.

Particularly Relevant Experience

Commercial and industrial client relationships in California.
Aerospace, manufacturing or energy-sector remediation programs.
Phase I and Phase II environmental investigations.
In-situ injection or other groundwater-remediation techniques.
Conceptual site models, aquifer testing and site characterization.
Groundwater or fate-and-transport modeling.
Leadership of large multidisciplinary investigation and remediation programs.
Responsibility for proposals, backlog development or account growth.

Location and Compensation

The role can be performed remotely within California

The anticipated base salary is $130,000–$180,000
, depending on experience. Additional flexibility may be available for an exceptional candidate, alongside a potentially substantial performance-based bonus.

Please apply directly for confidential consideration or contact Taylor at Harper Harrison for further information.

At Stantec, we approach every mining project we undertake—whether at the local, regional, or international level thoughtfully, and execute it with excellence across all project phases. We partner with our clients to design fit-for-purpose solutions that address their communities’ unique needs throughout the mining lifecycle. Our experts lead their fields and guide our work with technical excellence, an innovative spirit, and a vision for growth. We’re a place where you can apply your passion and collaborate with top talent on work that’s critical to our clients, our communities, and the industry at large.

Your Opportunity

Stantec is seeking qualified candidates for an Intermediate Level Hydrogeologist, reporting to an office in Salt Lake City, Reno, Denver or Phoenix (location is flexible). The primary focus of this position is to support hydrogeologic studies for our regional and international mining industry clients. The individual will engage complex projects related to industrial water supply, mine dewatering, acid rock drainage, metal leaching, mineral precipitation, pit lake chemistry, water-rock interactions, and mine permitting.

The successful candidate will work on challenging, high-impact projects within multi-disciplinary teams to design and execute baseline studies, feasibility studies, and other hydrogeological investigations to support client objectives. Travel will be required and some projects require visiting remote sites.

Your Key Responsibilities

Develop preliminary conceptual hydrogeological models to support field program design
Design and oversee implementation of hydrogeology field investigations including drilling and logging of overburden and bedrock core, sampling of soil, groundwater and bedrock
Design and oversee installation of monitoring wells, supply wells, dewatering wells, and vibrating wire piezometers
Design and oversee single well and multi-well aquifer test programs
Support development of numerical groundwater models to support dewatering requirements and environmental impact assessments
Prepare field data summary reports, including lithologic logs
Travel as required to various field sites with overnight travel sometimes required (valid driver’s license is required)
Follow safe work practices and adhere to company and client guidelines and policies for planning and executing work in a safe manner
Strong communication skills and collaborative working relationships with cross‑disciplinary teams

Education and Experience

A Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology or related discipline is required with a master’s degree preferred
Experience using GIS tools
Experience using hydrogeologic analytical tools for interpretation of aquifer test results
Experience using groundwater modeling tools such as MODFLOW or FEFLOW preferred, but not required
Minimum of 5 years of experience
Strong technical writing skills
Professional license (PG) or the ability to obtain a professional license
Exceptional organizational, technical, written and oral communication and attention to detail skills
Foreign language skills are a plus

Strong communication skills and collaborative working relationships with cross‑disciplinary teams

Experience using GIS tools
Experience using hydrogeologic analytical tools for interpretation of aquifer test results
